rationale: The AMLAS document (Example 32, pp. 34-36) explicitly describes the use of ROC curves and confusion matrices to evaluate performance for a retinal disease referral system. It states that varying a threshold on the ROC curve allows selection of an 'acceptable trade-off' and that 'the costs associated with mis-classification are not uniform'. The document concludes that 'a trade-off is therefore required between different metrics in order to form a judgement on the acceptability of the model’s performance in the given context of use'. This directly supports all parts of the claim within its stated scope, which is limited to the AMLAS clinical-referral example and explanatory evaluation pattern.
evidence_locators: S-RISK-005: PDF pp. 34-36, Activity 11 and Example 32 / Figure 11
limitations: This review verifies the claim against the provided AMLAS excerpt and its stated scope, which is limited to an explanatory clinical example. It does not assess the broader applicability of AMLAS methods to autonomous-road or aviation systems, nor does it evaluate the sufficiency of such methods for real-world safety claims.
